title: The Torn Tunic (Qamīs)
description: A fine Egyptian linen tunic with torn fabric fibers along the posterior shoulder seam. The central physical exhibit in the palace accusation.

scriptureReferences.text: A witness from her household testified: 'If his garment is torn from the front, she has spoken truth and he is of the liars. But if it is torn from the back, she has lied and he is truthful.'
She caught him by his garment, saying, 'Lie with me.' But he left his garment in her hand and fled. And when she saw that he had left his garment... she called to the men of her house.

forensicFinding: Posterior tearing demonstrates force exerted from behind while fleeing, directly corroborating defensive retreat.

title: Deposition of Grand Chamberlain Al-Aziz
description: Official chamberlain administrative roll documenting Yusuf's unblemished stewardship of the noble estate and private affairs.

scriptureReferences.text: The King asked the women: 'What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf?' They said: 'Allah forbid! We know no evil against him.' The wife of Al-Aziz said: 'Now truth is manifest: it was I who sought to seduce him.'
Joseph found favor in his sight and served him, and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

forensicFinding: The master's immediate reaction did not mandate execution—customary for domestic treason—proving lingering moral doubt.

title: Citrus Banquet Paring Knives
description: Bronze ceremonial fruit paring blades from the noble banquet of the city wives, cited as proof of irresistible awe.

scriptureReferences.text: She gave each of them a knife and said, 'Come out before them.' When they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands, saying, 'Allah forbid! This is not a human being; this is none but a noble angel!'

forensicFinding: Shows the societal pressure and palace gossip surrounding the household prior to formal detention.

title: Chamberlain Bronze Master Seal
description: The bronze ring seal granting unrestricted entry to inner storerooms and royal household ledgers.

scriptureReferences.text: He left all that he had in Joseph's charge, and because of him he had no concern about anything but the food he ate.

forensicFinding: Complete fiduciary trust was placed in the Hebrew overseer without co-signatory requirements.

title: Testimony of the Household Sage
description: Deposition recorded by a relation of the household who formulated the legal test of the torn garment.

scriptureReferences.text: And a witness from her family testified: 'If his garment is torn from the front...'

forensicFinding: Neutral domestic arbitrator proposed mathematical evidence rather than reliance on verbal oaths.

title: Royal Fortress Prison Ledger
description: Papyrus ledger from the fortress where the king's prisoners were bound, noting Yusuf's appointment as trustee inside.

scriptureReferences.text: Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison... but the Lord was with Joseph and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
Then it occurred to them after seeing the signs that they must imprison him for a time.

forensicFinding: Imprisonment was enacted for political expediency to silence noble scandal, not due to substantiated guilt.

title: Returned Silver in the Grain Sacks
description: Sealed pouches containing the exact silver shekels paid by the brothers, secretly replaced inside each sack mouth.

scriptureReferences.text: As one opened his sack... he saw his money in the mouth of his sack: 'My money has been returned! It is right here in my sack!'
Yusuf said to his servants: 'Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags so that they may recognize it when they return to their family, that perhaps they will come back.'

forensicFinding: Egyptian granary seals remained intact on the sacks, proving the treasure was deposited prior to convoy departure.

title: Memphis Granary Export Manifest
description: Imperial inventory roll documenting famine grain allocations granted per foreigner entering through Goshen.

scriptureReferences.text: When he had provided them with their provisions, he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?'

forensicFinding: One camel-load was allocated per individual; Benjamin's absence on trip one restricted the brothers' quota.

title: Canaanite Famine Starvation Plea
description: Testimony documenting desperate famine in Canaan, refuting the crown allegation of military espionage.

scriptureReferences.text: When Jacob learned that there was grain for sale in Egypt, he said to his sons... 'Go down and buy grain for us there, that we may live and not die.'

forensicFinding: The brothers entered through ten separate city gates to forage food quietly, misconstrued as hostile intelligence-gathering.

title: Detention Chains of Simeon
description: Iron shackle inventory recording Simeon detained as hostage while the others returned for Benjamin.

scriptureReferences.text: He turned away from them and wept. And he returned to them and spoke to them. And he took Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes.

forensicFinding: Hostage was kept in comfortable governor quarters rather than penal mines, indicating protective custody.

title: Governor's Secret Steward Order
description: Private command tablet instructing granary steward Menasseh to double provisions and conceal the silver.

scriptureReferences.text: The steward said: 'Peace be with you, do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasure in your sacks; I received your money.'

forensicFinding: Confirms intentional benevolence and moral trial engineered entirely from the executive bench.

title: Patriarch Jacob's Consignment Gift
description: Tribute jar containing Canaanite balm, honey, gum, myrrh, pistachio nuts, and almonds offered to appease the ruler.

scriptureReferences.text: Take some of the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry a present down to the man... take double the money with you.

forensicFinding: Substantiates honest merchant intent to repay any clerical error doublefold.

title: The Royal Divining Goblet (Siqāyah)
description: An engraved electrum goblet used by the vizier for drinking and divination, discovered inside Benjamin's grain sack.

scriptureReferences.text: A herald called out: 'O caravan! You are thieves!' They said: 'What is missing?' They replied: 'The king's drinking cup, and whoever brings it shall have a camel-load of grain.'
'Put my silver cup in the mouth of the sack of the youngest...' Is this not the cup my lord drinks from and uses for divination?

forensicFinding: Grain surrounding the goblet was completely unpacked and pristine, proving it was planted without Benjamin's knowledge.

title: Judah's Surety Bond & Plea
description: Formal personal bond by Judah offering his own life as permanent slave in exchange for Benjamin's liberation.

scriptureReferences.text: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a servant to my lord, and let the boy go back with his brothers.
They said: 'O Aziz! Indeed he has a father who is an old man, so take one of us in his place.' The eldest said: 'Do you not know that your father took an oath from you by Allah?'

forensicFinding: Proves the brothers reversed the historical crime of selling Joseph into slavery by sacrificing their freedom for Rachel's younger son.

title: Seven-Year Granary Imperial Decree
description: Royal decree granting Yusuf unilateral authority over Egyptian borders, grain reserves, and statutory jurisprudence.

scriptureReferences.text: You shall be over my house... only in regard to the throne will I be greater than you.

forensicFinding: Yusuf held full executive power to pardon, release, or sentence foreign nationals at will.

title: The False Blood Coat from Dothan
description: The colorful tunic dipped in goat blood twenty years prior, brought to Jacob to simulate predatory beast death.

scriptureReferences.text: And they came with his shirt stained with false blood. Jacob said: 'Nay, but your souls have enticed you to something. Patience is most fitting.'

forensicFinding: The shirt had no claw tears, which exposed the brothers' original deceit to Jacob.

title: Egyptian Divination Protocol Tablet
description: Temple register recording the ritual functions of the king's electrum silver cup in observing omens.

scriptureReferences.text: Joseph said to them: 'What deed is this that you have done? Do you not know that a man like me can indeed practice divination?'

forensicFinding: The cup theft carried diplomatic and sacred treason penalties under statutory Pharaonic code.

title: Decree of Full Imperial Pardon
description: The closing proclamation of Yusuf revealing his identity and settling Jacob's house in the fertile land of Goshen.

scriptureReferences.text: He said: 'No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.'
Joseph said to his brothers: 'I am Joseph! Does my father still live?'... 'Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.'

forensicFinding: Ultimate legal conclusion: reconciliation and sovereign preservation over vengeance.
